about: What a value typed by the user becomes when it is stored, by the rule docs/DECISIONS.md records
under "Single-line text is stored without surrounding whitespace, the rest as written".
stripToNull is a single-line value (a name, an account field, a host, a subject),
stripBlankLinesToNull a multi-line one (a note, a signature); null means no value.
Both implementations run every vector: StoredText (StoredTextTest, backend) and
frontend/src/lib/storedText.ts, so a rule changed in one and not the other fails a build.
Invisible characters are written as \u escapes on purpose: a reviewer cannot see them otherwise,
and an editor that turns one into a plain space would leave the vector passing and testing nothing.

vectors.why: ASCII spaces and a tab around a name go, the double space inside stays
A no-break space on both sides, as a word processor pastes it
A narrow no-break space and a figure space
A byte order mark pasted from a file goes from a single line; before the first line of a block it stays, like any indentation
An em space and an ideographic space
A line separator at the end
NEL stays: JavaScript's trim() keeps it, though Java's \p{IsWhite_Space} counts it
An information separator stays: String.strip() would remove it, JavaScript's trim() keeps it
A zero-width space is whitespace to neither
Whitespace inside a value stays, a no-break space included
The empty string is no value
A signature: the blank lines around it go, the indentation of its lines stays
Windows line ends, and lines of spaces alone before the text
A one-line note keeps a space it starts with
A line of no-break spaces alone before the text is a blank line
